src: Ken Krippene, Buried Treasure (1950), the 'golden outhouse' tale, as summarised in the Chicago Tribune, 8 May 1950, p. 20
Miami item (TN TreasureNet Treasure Legends thread 38771, 67635)
set.st: A 1950 press-agent tale: cattle buyer Felix Conway hid $200,000-$250,000 in gold in his back yard (or privy) in 1868 to keep it from his estranged wife. The Tribune item of 1950 was a notice of Ken Krippene's book Buried Treasure, which is where the tale comes from; no earlier record has been found.

George Gehrlach, who had lived like the poorest people in a humble cottage on North Cass Street, Portage, died on Saturday evening 13 June 1903. His daughters, Mrs. Paulina Felgenheuer and Mrs. Rebecca Manthey, claimed $6,000-7,000 in notes and mortgages and said the widow had appropriated it, and demanded a warrant. On 16 June Justice Heidt and District Attorney Andrews made an official search and dug up $4,890 in gold under the residence; the wire copies put the money under the kitchen floor at $5,450 with two notes from the daughters. Over $6,000 in property was recovered in all, and a bitter estate fight followed. The widow, Magdalena Gehrlach, lived on in Portage's Fifth Ward and left for Germany in 1904. Recovered by the estate; urban lot, no house number printed.
pinev: Street named (North Cass Street), no house number; pin on the north half of Cass St, Portage.
Widow in the Fifth Ward (1904 papers): fits the North Cass Street cottage; house number still unknown.
